recipes.name: Baked Scallops
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds bay scallops, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Pour melted butter into a 2-quart oval casserole dish; add scallops and spread to form an even layer.
Mix bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, minced garlic, onion powder, garlic powder, paprika, and parsley together in a small bowl: sprinkle over the scallops.
Bake scallops in the preheated oven until firm, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Scallops
raw_recipe.description: Baked scallops in a buttery sauce, topped with bread crumbs and seasoned with garlic, paprika, parsley and Parmesan make a terrific seafood main dish.

review.reviewBody: Much praise! After reading the reviews, I was nervous that I might mess this recipe up some how but even I got it right! I nixed the garlic powder and onion powder and used panko for the breadcrumbs. And even though some reviewers mentioned that their dish turned out soggy, I added extra butter anyway. Of course, the one day that I needed fresh scallops, our seafood market here at the beach was out! But frozen worked out just fine. Just let the bag thaw out in a bowl of cold water for about 30 minutes and then dry them between paper towels. The scallops turned out amazing. I am still getting compliments from my house! Thanks!

I halved the recipe since we only had 10 scallops and they turned out perfectly. I sprayed the ramekin with cooking spray, added the butter and put into the microwave to melt. Added the scallops and rolled them in the melted butter. We love garlic so I used a lil extra and more crushed parsley for looks. Even tho I generously covered the scallops with the topping, I had quite a bit leftover. I added this during the last 5 min of baking and thought of dabbing more butter onto the topping. So glad I didn't as it may have made the topping soggy. These were the best scallops we've ever had!

This recipe came out great! I did make a few changes though. I used sea scallops because we are lucky to get awesome ones here in southeastern Connecticut - right off the boats! I sprayed the casserole dish with cooking spray. Mixed the melted butter, minced garlic and scallops together to evenly coat. The combined bread crumbs, parsley, paprika and cheese and sprinkled over the scallops. I lightly sprayed the crumb mixture with butter flavored cooking spray. My husband and I loved it and I will definitely make it again!

Delicious and easy. Changes I made: 1. No breadcrumbs so replaced with hemp hearts (making it gluten free) 2. Substituted nutritional yeast for parmesan (to reduce dairy that I eat too much of) 3. NO minced garlic - seemed to me that the 1 tsp of powdered garlic was plenty 4. No parsley - had none on hand 5. Cooked an extra 5 minutes as some recommended 6. Did not use all the prepared mix, so saved about half to use again. I'll try it with baked fish next. I will definitely make this again - with my changes!

My husband is going carb free so we ditched the breadcrumbs. We melted the butter in a pan and added fresh garlic, wine, and lemon. We drizzled this all over the scallops and then added paprika, cayenne, parmesan, and parsley on top. 20 minutes was perfect. If I make this again, I would add more wine and lemon. Great recipe. The bay scallops are so delicate. I definitely prefer them to the larger ones.
I I liked it! I did marinate in sesame oil, garlic, ginger and teriyaki, before baking it.
Great recipe and easy. I dried the scallops and added fresh parsley at the end.

I doubled the sauce, and added a bed of angel hair pasta to the bottom of the casserole did before I began layering the ingredients. Also, I took the advice of many and went very light on the Old Bay Seasoning, and used fresh spinach. Thank you for sharing a delightful recipe. I was looking for something similar a delicious meal I had in NC. This one hit the spot! Yum!

I did a Keto modification by skipping the bread crumbs. Also, I used olive oil spray to coat the baking sheet. Then I thoroughly dried each scallop with a paper towel before placing onto the sprayed sheet. In a separate bowl I melted 5 tablespoons of butter and added all the rest of the ingredients to it except for Parmesan cheese. The butter became a little thickened and I was able to somewhat spread it all over the scallops. Cooked exactly as it is suggested in the recipe. Result - yummy juicy goodness! Great recipe!

I left out the butter altogether and simply sprayed the bottom of the glass pan with olive oil spray. Then also sprayed the top . Top cane out crunchy and no problems with sogginess. I thought it was five star without the butter and made for less calories and fat .

The flavor is good, but the bake time is way too high for bay scallops. Mine were a decent size, but were rubbery after 20 minutes of cooking. I sautéed the garlic in the butter first, coated the scallops in the butter, then cover in the dry ingredients. I put the Parmesan on top and it made a nice crust.
Super bland and bitter- salt and pepper are absolutely needed, more butter to be melted on top of breadcrumbs before going in. No call for lemon?

I made this for the fist time when having guests over. So glad I did, it was a huge hit. This is so much easier than pan frying and much less messy. Nice crisp and flavorful. This is definitely the best recipe I have found. And even better ,very little fishy smell in the house. I'm going to try this in my air fryer next.

Loved it. The combination is delicious. I did change the cheese to Mexican mixed cheese but I'm sure any cheese would do. Having the video helped because I never knew about the muscle that had to be removed to make it more tender.
This was very good according to the recipe. But, next time I think i’d prefer it with no bread crumbs & a little more garlic butter, or with about 1/3 cup of seasoned panko crumbs on top.
I left out the cloves of garlic and it was great. And I love garlic.
Very easy and very tasty! I served it with fettuccine and salad. A squeeze of lemon was perfect.

I made this tonight as directed except I used chunky garlic paste instead of fresh garlic. It. Was. Amazing. When I prepared it I thought that’s way too much topping, but after the dish came out of the oven and I ate some, it was perfect. I’ll make this again.
I could eat this until I popped! I would make this once a week if I could afford it.
